doc.title: Sherrie Maricle interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 18, 2001 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Keeping Diva's schedule together
summary: Members prioritize Diva around Broadway, wedding bands and other work; the lead trumpeter joined the Army blues band.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Is it hard to coordinate everybody’s schedule? I mean yours alone, but to get everybody together for rehearsals and to play gigs?

Yeah. I think people make it a priority because they like it and as we were saying before there’s not loads of places where you can get a chance to express yourself playing jazz. A lot of people in the group play Broadway shows, a lot of them play in wedding bands, some have their own bands, but you know there are clubs in New York that play for the door or then you make three dollars a night. I mean there are still fun jobs to do but it’s still amazing that people can play for the door. Yeah, they make Diva I think a priority and everybody’s pretty dedicated to it. Our lead trumpet player recently joined the Army. She’s the first woman lead trumpet player in a military band. She’s in the Army blues band.
Yeah so we’re having trouble getting her. Once in a while she can get free.
